codex_note:
## Codex adaptation and security boundary

This is a per-turn native Codex guidance adapter. It preserves the 23 playbooks and their principles, but it does not create a sticky mode or claim implicit future invocation. Read the selected playbook from the project-local mirror. Map the upstream question action to the host's optional user-input surface only for a genuine product or preference choice. Map the upstream task and delegation fields to native bounded delegation when exposed, keeping scope, selected model/effort, ownership, and proof with the coordinator. If delegation is unavailable, use the labeled sequential fallback. Keep model selection with model-capability-router and proof-path selection with proof-orchestrator. A heartbeat or automation is used only when explicitly requested.

This candidate remains unindexed. Finding review: bundled-script-review at scripts/**:n/a (bundled_executable_surface); executable-file at scripts/check-plan.mjs,scripts/worktree-audit.sh,scripts/orch/orch.ts,scripts/watch-pr/watch-pr:n/a (active_executable_surface); dependency-manifest-surface at scripts/package.json:n/a (active_dependency_surface). Do not install dependencies or activate the bundled scripts until code, dependency, and egress behavior is reviewed.
codex_rule: Respect native Codex model/effort, permissions and actual tool availability; no automatic Cursor runtime equivalence.
preserved_requirement: poteto's agent style for concise, detailed responses, deliberate subagents, unslopped prose, simple code, and verified work. Use for poteto, /poteto-mode, or requests to work in this style.
proof: Pinned source hash and deterministic renderer are static provenance. Focused tests exercise the 23-playbook registry, positive selection, missing-playbook fallback, malformed input, and the rendered frontmatter and security boundary.
reason: The adapter preserves the full source tree while making the runtime mapping, no-sticky boundary, native authority, and executable-script hold explicit.
